question: Which programme was restructured and renamed as ‘National Rural Employment Programme’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Food for Work Programme**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Food for Work Programme was restructured and renamed as the National Rural Employment Programme.
 
• This programme aimed to provide employment opportunities in rural areas through the creation of durable assets.
 
• It focused on the socio-economic development of rural areas by generating employment and improving infrastructure.
 
• The initiative was part of the Indian government's broader strategy to alleviate poverty in rural regions.
 
• Under this programme, workers were compensated with food grains in addition to wages, ensuring food security along with employment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP)**

 
 
• IRDP was aimed at providing self-employment opportunities to the rural poor through a mix of subsidy and credit.
 
• It focused on improving the income-generating capacity of target groups.
 
 
 
• **National Institute of Rural Development (NIRD)**
 
 
• NIRD is an autonomous organization under the Ministry of Rural Development.
 
• It provides training, research, and consultancy services in the field of rural development.
 
 
 
• **Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme (RLEGP)**
 
 
• RLEGP aimed to provide guaranteed employment to at least one member of every landless household up to 100 days in a year.
 
• The programme was later merged into the National Rural Employment Programme.
